content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: possible cross-tenant routing detected for customer HalleyCorp on dedicated-pool-13. Classification: potential tenant-isolation breach. Auto-tags: vpc, dedicated, routing, high-priority

maria (oncall-sre): Acked. I'm taking lead. quick question — is there an obvious spike in egress or any 5xx from the pool?

alex (eng-runtime): Seeing unusual `x-tenant-id` headers in audit logs for requests served by dp-13. Some requests with tenant B headers are hitting HalleyCorp backends. Suspect route programming or prefix overlap.

sam (oncall-eng): On it. I'm SSHing into control-plane to pull routing table and the latest config diff.

jamal (eng-platform): If this is routing-programming, we should cordon dp-13 ASAP to stop new allocations. Prepare to shift HalleyCorp to standby dedicated-pool-21. Need a quick capacity check.

chris (support): Heads-up: HalleyCorp account shows two customers reporting odd data traces in logs around 12:39 UTC. I'll hold comms until we have confirmed impact.

maria (oncall-sre): Commands I'm running now (sharing output as I go):
```
# check active routes on dp-13
redwoodctl routes list --pool dedicated-pool-13 --format json | jq '.routes[] | {prefix,owner,advertised_by}'
# inspect audit log for tenant header mismatch
grep "x-tenant-id" /var/log/redwood/audit/dp-13.log | grep -E "HalleyCorp|TenantB" | tail -n 200
```

alex (eng-runtime): Also check KV cache namespace mapping — if a prefix was accidentally mapped to the wrong tenant namespace it could serve stale KV caches across tenants. Run: `kv-map-inspect --pool dp-13 --prefix 10.42.0.0/16`

deploy-bot: Deployment event: route-manager v2.14.3 applied to dp-13 at 12:36:02 UTC by jamal.

tess (security): Important: collect full packet samples and preserve logs — we need chain-of-custody. Don't restart services that would rotate logs. If evidence shows data exposure, we'll need legal informed.

sam (oncall-eng): Found suspicious route advertisement: dp-13 has a /16 that overlaps HalleyCorp /24 and also matches a shared prefix used by TenantB due to a missing more-specific entry in the prefix table. Pasting snippet:
```
# routes dump (trimmed)
{ "prefix": "10.42.0.0/16", "owner": "platform-route-mgr", "advertised_by": "dp-13" }
{ "prefix": "10.42.5.0/24", "owner": "HalleyCorp", "advertised_by": "dp-13" }
{ "prefix": "10.42.0.0/20", "owner": "TenantB", "advertised_by": "dp-13" }
```
This looks like an accidental aggregation caused by the recent route-manager change.

jamal (eng-platform): I rolled the route-manager release earlier (deploy-bot msg). Possible bug in the prefix reconciliation: it sometimes emits a superset instead of leaving the more-specific in place when a pool restart happens. I'm pausing further route-manager jobs and can revert the change.

maria (oncall-sre): Mitigation plan (live):
- 12:41 UTC: Cordon dp-13 (no new allocations) — sam applied cordon.
- 12:42 UTC: Add explicit /24 for HalleyCorp to the route table to re-establish more-specific route.
- 12:44 UTC: Temporarily announce static ACL blocking TenantB->HalleyCorp flows at dp-13.
- 12:50 UTC: Start shifting HalleyCorp allocations to dedicated-pool-21 (warm pool).
Please confirm each step completed.

sam (oncall-eng): cordon done, ACL applied (iptables rule inserted mapping to DROP for TenantB source prefixes). Verified `conntrack` shows no new cross-tenant sessions after rule.

alex (eng-runtime): Added explicit /24 for HalleyCorp in route-store. Propagated. Observing routing table update and gracioius failover.

chris (support): Mia, please standby to draft a careful customer update. We should avoid language implying confirmed data exfil. Say: "We detected routing anomalies affecting traffic segmentation. We have applied mitigations and are investigating."

mia (customer-success): Acknowledged. I'll prep a message and hold until security sign-off.

tess (security): Evidence collection completed: packet capture and audit logs saved to /evidence/incidents/1987654321/. I also started a minimal impact data-access audit to enumerate any keys/objects that were served to mismatched tenant ids. Early look shows <10 requests with mismatched headers — collecting payloads now.

jamal (eng-platform): Reverted the problematic route-manager change to v2.14.2 and restarted daemon on control-plane. Confirming no further superset advertisements.

maria (oncall-sre): Traffic metrics — we've seen ~0.02% of total dp-13 requests affected, window ~12:36-12:46 UTC. We need cross-check from logging for 200 responses that included the wrong tenant id in the body.

alex (eng-runtime): KV namespace audit: found two `get` requests that returned keys from HalleyCorp namespace while serving requests tagged TenantB. Captured full payloads (stored with evidence).

tess (security): From preliminary evidence, this looks like accidental routing + namespace mapping exposure, not an intentional exploit. Impact limited in scope. We'll proceed with incident classification: P2 (customer-specific data exposure) and start escalation to legal and CISO.

chris (support): Preparing customer-facing note. Proposed short blurb: "We detected an internal routing configuration issue that may have allowed a small number of requests to reach incorrect backend namespaces. We have isolated the pool, reverted the faulty change, and are conducting a detailed review. We will follow up with findings and remedial actions." Any objections?

tess (security): Good. Add that we retained evidence and are performing a forensic audit. Don't promise exact counts yet.

maria (oncall-sre): Post-mitigation checks:
- route-table now correct (no overlapping /16).
- ACLs removed after explicit /24 fix applied.
- HalleyCorp active traffic moved to dp-21 and healthy.
- No new cross-tenant sessions after 12:46 UTC.
Please sign off on closure steps.

jamal (eng-platform): I will open a platform bug (PLAT-4876) to add stricter reconciliation tests and a safeguard preventing superset advertisements. Also adding an alert on route-manager that fires if a pool advertises a prefix that overlaps a more-specific owner prefix.

sam (oncall-eng): Running final scan for other pools with similar pattern... no other pools showing the pattern.

maria (oncall-sre): For the incident timeline and postmortem: I'll draft a blameless postmortem covering root cause (route-manager recon bug + rollout gap), impact (limited request set, HalleyCorp only), mitigations, and follow-ups (tests, rollback path, exec summary). Assigning to myself to produce within 72h.

tess (security): I'll coordinate evidence packet to Legal. CISO looped in.

chris (support): Customer message ready pending security sign-off. Will send once Mia confirms.

mia (customer-success): Security sign-off received, sending customer note now and will schedule a short sync with their engineering lead.

maria (oncall-sre): Closing the pager: confirmed containment and migration complete. Creating incident record and postmortem link once draft is ready. If anyone has additional artifacts, drop them in '/evidence/incidents/1987654321/'.

deploy-bot: Action log: route-manager rollback -> 12:53 UTC. dp-13 cordon removed at 13:10 UTC after full verification.

sam (oncall-eng): final check: `netstat` and `conntrack` clear, no stale sessions.

maria (oncall-sre): Thanks everyone. Handoff: I'll own the postmortem and timeline. Alex/jamal/sam/tess — please add technical appendices. Chris/mia — include customer timeline and message copies.

incident-bot: Pager resolved by maria at 13:12:10 UTC. Severity: P2. Followup required: postmortem, platform fix PLAT-4876, test coverage update.
